merger_description:
McCarroll's of Moss Vale Pty Ltd (**McCarroll’s**) (via a special purpose vehicle, MAG South Coast Pty Ltd) proposes to acquire, through two separate and independent transactions, substantially all of the assets (being all the assets necessary for the operation of the business) of:

* the motor vehicle dealership business owned by Kinghorn Motors Pty Ltd (**KMG**)
* the motor vehicle dealership business owned by Country Motor Company Pty Ltd (**CMC**).

As part of the same transactions, McCarroll's (via McCarroll Property Holdings Pty Ltd) proposes to acquire the land on which the KMG and CMC motor dealership businesses are operated.

(together, the **Acquisitions**)

determination_table_content.details:
McCarroll's of Moss Vale Pty Ltd (McCarroll’s) (via a special
purpose vehicle, MAG South Coast Pty Ltd) proposes to acquire,
through two separate and independent transactions, substantially all
of the assets (being all the assets necessary for the operation of the
business) of:
• the motor vehicle dealership business owned by Kinghorn
Motors Pty Ltd (KMG)
• the motor vehicle dealership business owned by Country Motor
Company Pty Ltd (CMC).
As part of the same transactions, McCarroll's (via McCarroll Property
Holdings Pty Ltd) proposes to acquire the land on which the KMG
and CMC motor dealership businesses are operated.
(together, the Acquisitions)

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, McCarroll's, sits within the broader McCarroll's
Automotive Group. McCarroll's is a new and used vehicle retailing
business that operates 15 franchised automotive dealerships across
10 locations in the following primary market areas (PMAs): Sydney,
North Shore, Hornsby and Newcastle. These PMAs are in
metropolitan Sydney and the Newcastle region.
McCarroll’s represents 15 Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)
vehicle brands as an authorised dealer: Alfa Romeo, Fiat, BYD, GWM,
Leap Motor, Lexus, Porsche, Ferrari, Maserati, Volkswagen, Volvo,
Geely, RAM, Jeep and Mazda. McCarroll’s also supplies OEM spare
parts, aftermarket servicing and finance solutions.
KMG is a new and used vehicle retailing business that operates 2
franchised automotive dealerships in the Nowra PMA. KMG
represents 2 OEM vehicle brands as an authorised dealer: Ford and
Volkswagen. KMG also supplies OEM spare parts, aftermarket
servicing and finance solutions.
CMC is a new and used vehicle retailing business that operates 3
franchised automotive dealerships in Bomaderry, NSW (also located
within the Nowra PMA). CMC represents three OEM vehicle brands
as an authorised dealer: Hyundai, Isuzu and GWM. CMC also
supplies OEM spare parts, aftermarket servicing and finance
solutions.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
McCarroll’s, the acquirer, is not active in the Nowra area or broader
Illawarra-Shoalhaven region, where KMG and CMC are located. As
such, the ACCC does not consider there is an existing relevant
geographic overlap between McCarroll’s and the target dealerships.
McCarroll’s closest dealerships to Nowra are in the Sydney suburb
of Alexandria, which is approximately 146km from the Nowra PMA.
However, KMG and CMC overlap in Nowra (within the Illawarra-
Shoalhaven region) in the supply of:
• new vehicles
• used vehicles
• OEM spare parts
• aftermarket servicing
• automotive finance services.
KMG and CMC do not overlap on an intra-brand basis.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, market inquiry feedback, and publicly available
information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect, as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
Regarding the supply of new vehicles
• The Acquisitions are likely to give rise to a moderate
increase in concentration in the supply of new cars in the
Nowra area.
• However, the merged firm would face competition from
multiple alternative suppliers of new cars, both on an intra-
brand and inter-brand basis.
Regarding the supply of used vehicles
• The merged firm would face competition from multiple
alternative suppliers of used cars.
Regarding the supply of aftermarket servicing and OEM spare parts
• Given KMG and CMC do not overlap on an intra-brand basis,
they are not likely to be close competitors in the supply of
aftermarket servicing and OEM spare parts, which
dealerships generally only provide for the OEM brands they
supply.
Regarding the supply of automotive finance services
• The merged firm would face competition from multiple
alternative suppliers of automotive finance services.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
